title: Nebraska: Defense That Ate Saturdays
description: Black practice jerseys, a Wyoming import's defense, and the unit that made Saturdays mean. Go Deep into Husker D lore.
imageHint: Black practice jerseys that became a statewide identity

questions.question: Nebraska's defense is known statewide by what nickname—taken from the color of their practice jerseys?
questions.explanation: Only defensive players who earned a starting job got the black jersey in practice. Offense wore white. The name stuck harder than any slogan the marketing department ever wrote.

questions.question: The Blackshirts tradition of those practice jerseys became sacred under which head coach—the mountain-west hire who rebuilt the program?
questions.explanation: Devaney brought the black-jersey hierarchy with him. Walk-ons still tell the story: you don't buy a Blackshirt—you earn it.

questions.question: Under Devaney's longtime successor, which defensive coordinator ran the Blackshirts from 1982 through the mid-90s title years?
questions.explanation: McBride's units were mean, multiple, and deeply local. When fans say "Blackshirt football," they're usually remembering his rooms as much as any single All-American.

questions.question: McBride's 1995 Blackshirts helped a national-title team that scored 50-plus a game—about how many points per game did that defense allow (nearest whole number)?
questions.explanation: About 14.5 including the Fiesta Bowl (12-game book); regular-season charts sat near 13.6. A 50-point offense married to a stingy front—mismatch factory.

questions.question: While that mid-90s Blackshirt front held opponents near 14 a game, which disruptive defensive end—later a Rams Super Bowl champion—became a face of the unit?
questions.explanation: Wistrom was a two-time All-American across the mid-90s title window, then won a Super Bowl with St. Louis. Suh's Outland/Nagurski year came a generation later, in 2009.

deeperMode.title: Go Deeper: More Blackshirt Blood
deeperMode.description: Names the Tunnel Walk crowd still chants

questions.question: Which Nebraska linebacker won the 1993 Butkus Award before the mid-90s title run?
questions.hint: Later an ESPN analyst and athletic director

questions.question: In 2009, which defensive tackle—nicknamed "Baby Giraffe" in Lincoln—won the Outland and Bronko Nagurski awards as a Blackshirt?
questions.hint: Went No. 2 overall to Detroit the next spring

easterEgg.title: You earn it
easterEgg.text: In the Devaney years and after, black jerseys weren't merchandise. Defensive starters got them for practice; everyone else watched. The nickname outlived the laundry rule.
